opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is full-time Analyst. Requested write to Payroll; full-time employees can have up to write (admin only if role owns the system). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E026 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The HR and Security notes conflict on employment type (HR: full_time; Security: contractor, both looked up in their own databases). Security's database additionally shows basic security training. Under the access policy, a contractor with basic training has a maximum of read (write requires advanced training). The requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum of read.
